acceptance_criteria.given: the stream lines measured today: an Agent tool_use, then a Bash tool_use and its tool_result with parent_tool_use_id set to the Agent call's id
acceptance_criteria.then: the Bash tool_use and tool_result payloads carry parent_call_id; the Agent call's payload carries none

acceptance_criteria.given: a run whose agent_outputs hold that Agent call (description 'count files') and the subagent's Bash call, and a pending permission request for the Bash call's tool_use_id
acceptance_criteria.then: the request's subagent is {call_id: the Agent call's id, description: 'count files'}; a request for an ordinary call reads subagent null

acceptance_criteria.given: a pending request whose subagent description is 'count files'
acceptance_criteria.then: it reads 'From a subagent: count files'; a request with no subagent shows no such line

acceptance_criteria.given: a scratch Hub and a Haiku agent under Ask me
acceptance_criteria.then: the listed permission request names the subagent's description
acceptance_criteria.when: the agent delegates a file write to a subagent

design: D1 Read-time join, no column: agent_outputs already holds every tool_use with its call_id and input; the list route reads the run's tool_use rows once and maps request.tool_use_id -> parent_call_id -> the Agent call's input description. D2 parent_call_id is set by parse_claude_line on the events it builds from a line, so every Claude path gets it. D3 The card line sits under the kind label, muted, so a subagent request is recognisable at a glance and an ordinary one is unchanged.
problem: F679 (research 2026-10-01 §2, re-measured 2026-10-18 on CC 2.1.301): every tool call a Claude subagent makes streams with a top-level parent_tool_use_id naming the parent's Agent call, and since CC 2.1.285 a subagent's permission request reaches --permission-prompt-tool, so under Ask me the operator answers it. The Hub reads parent_tool_use_id nowhere (0 hits in hub/hub): the card and the conversation show a subagent's Write or Bash as the agent's own call, though its prompt was written by the agent, not the operator. The paper Approval Laundering (arXiv 2609.38983) names this Delegation laundering.

requirements.rationale: The join key exists in the stream and is the only record of who made the call.
requirements.statement: A Claude tool_use or tool_result event from a line carrying parent_tool_use_id MUST record it as parent_call_id in its payload.

requirements.rationale: The stream line can arrive after the request opens, so a value fixed at write time could be missing; the card polls every 3 s.
requirements.statement: A permission request listed for the operator MUST carry a subagent field naming the parent call's id and its description when its tool call was made by a subagent, resolved when the list is read, and null otherwise.

requirements.rationale: The operator decides in seconds; who is asking is part of what they decide.
requirements.statement: The permission card MUST say a request is from a subagent and show the delegation's description, and the conversation MUST mark a subagent's tool call as one.

in_scope: The Claude parser carries parent_tool_use_id as parent_call_id on tool_use and tool_result payloads
GET /permission-requests resolves, at read time, the subagent a request's tool call came from: the parent Agent call's id and description
The permission card says 'From a subagent' with that description; the conversation's tool row is marked as a subagent's
non_goals: Nesting a subagent's calls under the Agent call in the timeline (backlog)
Copilot subagents (its ACP client has its own path)
Any change to what is approved or refused: this is attribution, not enforcement
A database column: the join is resolved on read from agent_outputs

summary: A Claude subagent's tool calls carry the Agent call they came from; the permission card says it is from a subagent and names the delegation, and the conversation's call row says so too.
